TERMINOLOGY · qeva:1:chaos@2

Chaos

A family of precise but non-equivalent dynamical notions rather than one universal predicate.

editorialdynamics · chaos

PLAIN

The idea

“Chaos” has several rigorous definitions. QEVA should name the definition being used instead of treating the word as self-explanatory.

EXACT

The compact statement

QEVA Protocol 0.2 assigns no universal predicate Chaos(T). A record claiming chaos must identify a contextual criterion (for example a named topological, measure-theoretic, symbolic, or metric definition) and state its hypotheses.

EXAMPLE

A map may satisfy sensitive dependence while failing some stronger named chaos criterion.

BOUNDARY / CAVEAT

Popular descriptions such as “random-looking” or “small errors grow” are not by themselves mathematical definitions of chaos.
